title: Gradient of a parallel line
source: Theory P1-3.2 Quick check 1 (parallel to y=5x-3); new integer gradients
stem: Find the gradient of a straight line parallel to \(y={m|int}x-3\).

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Parallel lines have equal gradients, so the gradient of a straight line is {A|int}.
steps.note: A equals m. Original m=5 gives 5.

title: Product of perpendicular gradients
source: Theory P1-3.2 Quick check 2 (product -1); constant identity
stem: The product of the gradients of two perpendicular lines is required. What is that product?

steps.name: A
steps.note: A is -1 for every seed. The dummy parameter k is unused in the answer.

title: Perpendicular to a line of gradient 1
source: Theory P1-3.2 Quick check 3 (perpendicular gradient -1); constant
stem: A line has gradient \(1\). What is the gradient of a straight line perpendicular to it?

title: A given line is perpendicular to AB

source.note: 9709/13/M/J/15 Question 7(ii) only [4]. Official QP and official MS. The opening sentence of Q7 is included so that the part is self-contained.

stem:
This question is 9709/13/M/J/15 Question 7(ii) only, taken from the official QP.

The point A has coordinates (p, 1) and the point B has coordinates (9, 3p + 1), where p is a constant.

(ii) For the case in which the line with equation 2x + 3y = 9 is perpendicular to AB, find the value of p. [4]

steps.name: B
steps.text_tex: The gradient of the given line is \(-\dfrac{2}{3}\).

steps.name: M1
steps.note: Official MS: M1, attempt using m1 m2 = -1.

steps.name: M2
steps.note: Official MS: M1 (includes previous M1); or a vector dot product equal to 0.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Official MS: A1. Independent: gradient of AB is 3p/(9-p); set equal to 3/2 gives 2*3p=3(9-p), 6p=27-3p, 9p=27, p=3. Last step is A.

contexts.note: Stem taken from the official QP PDF (UCLES 2015), Question 7(ii) only. Official MS reproduced mark by mark. Paper/self-mark.
